_Privacy first, on your own devices, no copy held_

# Your records never leave the room.

Aveneg Technologies makes software for watch collectors. Watch Vault Archive and Watch Vault Tracker keep your records on your own computer, iPhone or iPad.

[See the products](https://avenegtechnologies.com/products/) [About the company](https://avenegtechnologies.com/about/)

_What we publish_

## Two products, each with its own site.

### Watch Vault Archive

_In development, coming Early 2027_

Part of the Watch Vault Archive watch list: three watches, each shown with a photograph, its maker and its model.

Illustrative data, not a real collection.

Documents the watches a collector owns.

Desktop software for a collection’s appraisals, service history, provenance and succession. Aveneg cannot read, recover or hand over what you record in it.

- For: Mac and Windows

[Visit watchvaultarchive.com](https://watchvaultarchive.com)

### Watch Vault Tracker

_In development, coming Early 2027_

The Watch Vault Tracker Today screen on an iPhone: a grid of drawn watches under the line “Tap the watch you’re wearing”, with the first watch ticked.

An illustration, not a screenshot.

Records the watches a collector wears.

Open it, tap the photograph of the watch on your wrist, and the watch, the date and the time are kept. Every feature is free for watch collectors: no subscription, no advertising, no trial.

- For: iPhone, iPad and Mac

[Visit watchvaulttracker.com](https://watchvaulttracker.com)

The two are separate products, and neither requires the other.

_Products_

# What we publish.

Aveneg Technologies is building two products for watch collectors. They are separate products, and neither requires the other.

## Watch Vault Archive

_In development, coming Early 2027_

Watch Vault Archive is desktop software that documents what a collector owns.

It is built for record-keeping over the long term. Its records are encrypted at rest with a key only their owner holds, and the software works offline. Aveneg Technologies cannot read, recover or hand over that data.

- For: Mac and Windows
- Records: Appraisals, service history, provenance and succession
- Kept: On your own computer
- Privacy: No account with us. No copy held by Aveneg.

[Visit watchvaultarchive.com](https://watchvaultarchive.com)

[Watch Vault Archive Terms of Service](https://watchvaultarchive.com/terms) [Watch Vault Archive Privacy Policy](https://watchvaultarchive.com/privacy)

The Watch Vault Archive application: a list of watches on the left, and one watch’s record open on the right showing its identification and acquisition details.

Illustrative data, not a real collection.

## Watch Vault Tracker

_In development, coming Early 2027_

Watch Vault Tracker is an app for iPhone, iPad and Mac that records the watches a collector wears.

Open it, tap the photograph of the watch on your wrist, and the watch, the date and the time are kept. We don’t collect any information about your collection: your records and photographs are kept on your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Every feature is free, with no subscription, no advertising and no trial; there is a place to leave an optional tip, and a tip unlocks nothing.

- For: iPhone, iPad and Mac
- Records: Each watch worn, with its date and time
- Kept: On your iPhone, iPad or Mac
- Privacy: No account with us. No copy held by Aveneg.
- Cost: Free for watch collectors

[Visit watchvaulttracker.com](https://watchvaulttracker.com)

[Watch Vault Tracker Terms of Service](https://watchvaulttracker.com/terms) [Watch Vault Tracker Privacy Policy](https://watchvaulttracker.com/privacy)

The Watch Vault Tracker Today screen on an iPhone: a grid of drawn watches under the line “Tap the watch you’re wearing”, with the first watch ticked.

An illustration, not a screenshot. The watches are drawn; in the app they are your own photographs.

Each product is licensed under its own documents, published on its own site, and those documents can differ from one product to the next. This website’s own [Terms of Service](https://avenegtechnologies.com/terms/) and [Privacy Policy](https://avenegtechnologies.com/privacy/) cover avenegtechnologies.com only.

_About_

# A software company built around one idea.

The idea is that a record of something valuable stays where its owner put it, and nowhere else.

## Why

A record of something valuable is worth protecting like the thing itself. Held on a company’s server, it can be exposed in ways its owner never sees: a breach at the provider, a demand served on the company instead of the person, a service that closes and takes years of entries with it. Software that keeps the record on the owner’s own device removes those risks by removing the server.

## How we build

Privacy comes first. In every product the records are kept on the owner’s own device; the company keeps no customer accounts and holds no copy. The rest is particular to each product. Watch Vault Archive is encrypted at rest with a key only its owner holds, so the company cannot read, recover or hand over that data. With Watch Vault Tracker, the company collects no information about a collection.

## What we publish

The company is building two products for watch collectors. Watch Vault Archive documents what a collector owns; Watch Vault Tracker records what a collector wears. They are separate products, and neither requires the other.

[See the products](https://avenegtechnologies.com/products/)

## What comes next

The products today are for watch collectors. The same approach will serve other collector communities later.

## Particulars

Aveneg Technologies, LLC is the publisher of both products. The company’s address, registration and email addresses are on the [Contact](https://avenegtechnologies.com/contact/) page.

_Legal_

# Privacy Policy

Last updated September 27, 2026

This policy covers avenegtechnologies.com only — the corporate website you are reading now. It does not cover any software the Company publishes. Each product has its own, separate Privacy Policy, linked from its entry on the [Products](https://avenegtechnologies.com/products/) page, that describes how that product handles data.

The short version: this site sets no cookies and has no accounts or forms. Our host, Cloudflare, provides standard server logs and basic, cookie-free traffic analytics (such as page views and performance). We don’t use them to identify you. If you never email us, we hold no other information about you.

## 1. What we collect from this site

Very little. This site is static: no accounts, no forms and no cookies. Cloudflare, which hosts it, measures aggregate traffic with cookie-free analytics.

Our hosting provider, Cloudflare, generates standard web server logs as an ordinary part of serving any website (for example, IP address and request timing, for security and reliability purposes). We do not access or analyze these logs as a matter of routine, and they are not used to build a profile of you.

## 2. If you email us

If you write to [info@avenegtechnologies.com](mailto:info@avenegtechnologies.com) or [legal@avenegtechnologies.com](mailto:legal@avenegtechnologies.com), we receive your email address and whatever you send. We use it only to respond to you. We do not add you to a mailing list, sell it, or share it with anyone, other than the infrastructure that delivers the email to us in the first place (see below).

## 3. Third parties

This site is hosted and its email is routed by Cloudflare, Inc., which operates the infrastructure that serves these pages and delivers mail sent to our addresses. Cloudflare’s own privacy policy governs its handling of data in that role.

## 4. Children

This site is not directed to children, and we do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 13.

## 5. Changes

We may update this policy from time to time. The date at the top of this page reflects the version currently in effect.

## 6. Contact

Questions about this policy: [legal@avenegtechnologies.com](mailto:legal@avenegtechnologies.com)
